title: Peary North Pole Claim
summary: Robert Peary, with Matthew Henson and a small team, claimed to have reached the North Pole on 6 April 1909. A National Geographic Society committee endorsed his account, but Frederick Cook also claimed the pole, and doubts about Peary's proof persist today.

uncertainty.note: Date is the claimed day; whether the pole was reached is disputed.

where.modern_name: Arctic Ocean, near the geographic North Pole (proxy pin at 90°N; actual position of the party unverified)
where.historical_name: Arctic sea ice, no sovereign territory

importance.justification: Contested claim to the first arrival at the North Pole, involving a congressional honour and a rival claim.

sources.title: Commander Robert Peary's handwritten calculations at the North Pole, April 6, 1909
Peary and Henson Reach the North Pole

reviewer_note: Pin is a proxy at 90N, not a verified position. Only two publishers; Capitol page gives Peary's recorded latitude 89°57′11″ and says experts doubt the final run.
